claim: What a user teaches an agent (a fact, a rule, a procedure) is a typed record read conservatively from what was said
gate: no teaching read from a non-teaching on an authored set; the reader finds the teachings of natural phrasings

claim: A taught fact, correction, procedure or rule is applied in a new session; a corrected fact stays corrected; a forgotten one stays forgotten; unrelated answers are unchanged
gate: pre-registered: lower 95% bound >= 0.80 per kind with untaught < 0.20; leak and disturbance checks pass

claim: A model reads teachings that plain phrase matching misses, with few false readings
gate: found share and false-reading count on the test split of authored utterances

claim: Teaching works by voice: spoken correction, spoken confirmation, changed next answer, spoken retraction
gate: scripted spoken conversations pass their checks end to end (three conversations, one synthetic voice)

claim: Lessons are a formal typed account of spoken feedback with a safe application rule
gate: extraction F1 on a frozen held-out utterance set; no lesson from a non-directive

claim: A lexicon lesson fixes a mispronounced word and generalizes across sentences
gate: human-rated pronunciation rises; no regression on untaught words (TOST)

claim: One spoken example lets the voice imitate delivery in context
gate: speaker similarity up; WER not worse; humans prefer

claim: Feedback-driven RL beats supervised and untouched baselines
gate: human blind preference sign test; WER and similarity guards

claim: The closed loop removes corrected errors without regressions
gate: corrected-item error falls; held-out unchanged within margin; rollback works

claim: The agent is usable by voice: tools, latency, disclosure
gate: first sound p50 <= 1.5 s and p95 <= 2.0 s over >=3 repeats on an idle card; tool task success within margin of text input

claim: The persona is a trained adapter
gate: adapter beats base and prompted base on the frozen exam
TOST equivalence on the frozen exam (M4 gate not met)
